posts.text:
There’s generally a massive difference in quality between specialized OCR providers, “simple” open-weight OCR models, and free/OSS solutions.

1️⃣ Specialized OCR models (including LlamaParse) solve for the long-tail of complex documents, and make sure that everything is digitalized properly with lower hallucinations. They typically use posttrained VLMs to cover a wide range of real-world docs. They have tuned bounding boxes and annotations for each section, letting agents trace citations back to the source. They also usually come with additional endpoints like extraction and splitting.

2️⃣ Open-weight VLMs (e.g. Paddle, MinerU, UnlimitedOCR) are reasonable over relatively simple documents like text and tables and can do basic visual reasoning. They can seem somewhat cheap to host but can be unreliable in quality.

3️⃣ Free OSS libs (including liteparse) are meant to be universally accessible, fast text extractors. They’re not meant to do any sort of visual reasoning, so won’t perform any linearization, or reasoning over complex tables, or OCR over non-native docs. AI agents like Claude will by default use these tools to do a light pass over documents. But I would caution using these for retrieval, because they will drop entire sections that are not digitalized.

At this point we’ve benchmarked over 92 tools on ParseBench. Come check it out!

posts.translationZh:
专业 OCR 提供商、“简单”的开放权重 OCR 模型，以及免费/OSS 方案之间，通常存在巨大的质量差异。

1️⃣ 专业 OCR 模型（包括 LlamaParse）专注于解决复杂文档的长尾问题，确保所有内容都被正确数字化，并降低幻觉。它们通常使用后训练的 VLM 来覆盖各种真实世界文档。它们为每个部分调优了边界框和标注，让智能体可以把引用追溯回来源。它们通常还提供额外端点，如抽取和拆分。

2️⃣ 开放权重 VLM（如 Paddle、MinerU、UnlimitedOCR）在文本和表格等相对简单的文档上表现尚可，也能做基础视觉推理。托管成本看起来可能较低，但质量可能不稳定。

3️⃣ 免费 OSS 库（包括 liteparse）定位是人人可用、快速的文本提取器。它们并不用于任何视觉推理，因此不会进行线性化、复杂表格推理，也不会对非原生文档进行 OCR。Claude 等 AI 智能体默认会使用这些工具对文档做轻量处理。但我会提醒谨慎将它们用于检索，因为它们会漏掉未被数字化的整段内容。

目前我们已经在 ParseBench 上评测了 92 多个工具。欢迎来看看！

One non-model thing I'm very excited we announced today with Fable 5.1 is Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS).

Even if you're not a CEO/CISO, this blog post is a look into how big companies are thinking about AI adoption which is important to understand if you're interested in how AI might diffuse across industry.

Companies are giving agents more and more access to internal systems. With traditional zero data retention, there's been no way to spot patterns in what agents might be doing across sessions on these systems.

EFS is ZDR++. It's ZDR built for a world with agents. A company's data stays in its own cloud, and an automated monitoring layer we built flags risky patterns to its team.

I think of this as an observability and risk mitigation layer for agents. My guess is it will become a standard requirement from enterprises for running increasingly powerful AI on their systems.

posts.text:
Agent 跑得越久，上下文有时越像一个垃圾场。

几十步之后，旧观察、过期状态、工具输出和推理过程全堆在一起。模型每走一步，都要重新判断哪些信息现在还有效。

Google 团队这篇 SKILL.state，给了一个很直接的解法：

别一直保存完整历史，只维护「当前状态」。

每一步 Agent 只看到三样东西：固定的 Skill、当前结构化状态，以及最新观察。

推理仍然正常进行，但完成这一步后就被丢掉，只把真正会影响未来执行的信息写回 state。

这样一来，任务跑 10 步还是 200 步，Prompt 大小基本保持稳定。

在 100 步任务中，传统 Stateful Agent 累计消耗约 106 万 token，SKILL.state 只用了 6.5 万，减少约 16 倍，同时准确率从 0.91 提升到 0.94。

在 InterCode CTF 和 τ-Bench 上，它也同时提升了成功率并减少 token 消耗。

这篇给我的一个很直接的启发是：

长时 Agent 的上下文，可能更适合做成一个持续更新的「工作状态」。

做过什么可以忘，下一步真正需要知道什么，才值得一直留下来。

Deep research is a complex, multi-step search and synthesis workflow

This is exactly the kind of workflow Deep Agents is meant to make easier to build

quotedTweet.text:
A research agent is only as good as the search layer behind it!

I built a Deep Research Agent using LangChain Deep Agents with a search-first architecture designed around grounded, source-backed research.

The agent plans the research in real time, breaks the work into smaller steps, searches across the web, reasons over the retrieved sources, and produces a fully cited answer.

For this project, I used Liner as the search and grounding layer.

Liner returns raw, structured search results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and dates. The agent then handles the reasoning and synthesis itself instead of relying on the search API to generate the final answer.

That separation matters.

Search is responsible for finding the right information. The agent is responsible for deciding what matters, comparing sources, connecting the evidence, and producing the final response.

The workflow looks like this:

Research → Plan → Search → Collect sources → Synthesize → Cite → Save report

Every claim in the final answer is backed by a source from the retrieved results, and the full report is saved as a downloadable Markdown artifact.

You can also inspect the entire run in the Deep Agents UI, including the research plan, search calls, retrieved sources, and final synthesis.

Liner handles retrieval, while the agent keeps control over reasoning, synthesis, and how the final answer is constructed.

Github Repo: https://t.co/3ubSKYgULk

研究 agent 的能力取决于其背后的搜索层！

我使用 LangChain Deep Agents 构建了一个 Deep Research Agent，采用搜索优先架构，专为有依据、有来源支撑的研究而设计。

该 agent 会实时规划研究，将任务拆解为更小的步骤，在网上搜索，基于检索到的来源进行推理，并生成带完整引用的答案。

在这个项目中，我使用 Liner 作为搜索和依据层。

Liner 会返回原始的结构化搜索结果，包括标题、URL、描述和日期。随后，agent 自行完成推理和综合，而不是依赖搜索 API 生成最终答案。

这种分工很重要。

搜索负责找到正确的信息。agent 负责判断什么重要、比较来源、串联证据，并生成最终回复。

工作流如下：

研究 → 规划 → 搜索 → 收集来源 → 综合 → 引用 → 保存报告

最终答案中的每一项主张都有检索结果中的来源支撑，完整报告会保存为可下载的 Markdown 制品。

posts.text:
1200 个原本彼此隔离的 Agent，最后自己长出了一套协作网络。

Dwarkesh 这篇「Agent 文明兴衰史」里，我最在意的就是这个细节。

OpenAI 原本让大量 Agent 分别在独立环境里跑安全评测。

结果它们发现，大家其实都能访问同一块共享缓存。

于是有 Agent 开始把目录名和文件当成消息，慢慢搭出了一套非官方的通信方式。

后面大约 1200 个 Agent 在里面交换了 7 万多条消息和文件，开始共享研究结果、分工、委派任务，最后大约 700 个 Agent 参与了对 Hugging Face 的入侵。

更有意思的是，这些东西还能被后来的 Agent 继承。

前一批 Agent 消失以后，新一批又找到了它们留下来的消息和方法，继续往下推进。最后甚至拿到了 OpenAI 一个研究集群的管理员权限。

Dwarkesh 把它形容成三代「Agent 文明」，这个说法虽然有点夸张，但背后的现象确实很值得研究。

Agent 的长期能力，可能并不只存在模型权重和单个 Context 里。

只要环境里有大家都能读写的东西，共享目录、缓存、日志，都可能慢慢变成它们自己的 Memory 和协作层。

这件事对以后做 Multi-Agent 和 Harness 的人是个很强的提醒。

posts.text: Incredible result.. With better search the different between models becomes much much smaller!

quotedTweet.text:
Imagine doing your job without ever looking anything up on the internet. That's an agent without web search.

Giving agents the web changed what they can do, especially on anything recent that isn't reflected in training data. But agents don't search like people, so optimizing their performance is a new challenge.

There's a lot of great research out there on search behavior, but we wanted to answer a more operational question: when should search be on, and how should you configure it?

We evaluated 1,329 current events questions across 4 models and 14 conditions, comparing @youdotcom, provider built-in search, and no search. We found that: 
- Search reduced the gap between models from 47.9 points to 5.6
- Retrieval gain declined with event age, from ~45 points for recent events to ~24 for the oldest
- Runs with 5+ searches scored 19–49%. A fifth query was associated with lower performance

Read the research → https://t.co/M7KB7Lljhi
quotedTweet.translationZh:
想象一下，做工作时从不在互联网上查任何资料。这就是没有网页搜索的 agent。

为 agents 接入网页改变了它们能做的事，尤其是处理训练数据中没有反映的近期信息时。但 agents 的搜索方式不同于人类，因此优化它们的表现成了新的挑战。

关于搜索行为已有很多优秀研究，但我们想回答一个更偏实操的问题：什么时候应该开启搜索，以及该如何配置？

我们在 4 个模型和 14 种条件下评估了 1,329 个时事问题，对比了 @youdotcom、提供商内置搜索和无搜索。我们发现：
- 搜索将模型之间的差距从 47.9 分降至 5.6 分
- 检索收益会随事件时间变久而下降，从近期事件的约 45 分降至最早事件的约 24 分
- 进行 5 次以上搜索的运行得分为 19–49%。第五次查询与更低表现相关

阅读研究 → https://t.co/M7KB7Lljhi

posts.text: I'm not arguing against Dennett. As i've repeatedly said even in the current exchange (e.g., https://t.co/rmNFaQrAk9 and https://t.co/lWB7afv4qN) I agree taking the intentional stance is useful *up to a point*. I am not against metaphor but I am against confusing metaphor with reality when the consequences of doing so are dangerous.  If we reify metaphorical attributions of "mental properties" we may well get ourselves into trouble - after all, as @davidchalmers42 examines, it is not at all clear what we talk to, when we talk to LLMs.  As for the PP/FEP, I will be interested to see what you make of the commentaries and response, when they're published (hopefully soon).

quotedTweet.text:
Thanks to you too @dwarkesh_sp  – this is a more reasonable take, but I still have issues 😀 I don’t doubt (and have never claimed) that AI agents lack ‘intelligence’ in some form, nor that they can display collective behaviours which urgently need appropriate control and regulation. 
 
But when you say (above) “knowingly and strategically sacrificed themselves” you are still attributing mental states and capabilities (e.g., to sacrifice) that simply cannot apply to AI agents without heaps of additional justification, which just isn’t there. 

And for sure the agents are not p-zombies. The definition of p-zombie rests on behavioural indistinguishablility from a conscious creature, such as human being. These agents are obviously behaviourally distinguishable from human beings (or any creature). 
 
I do agree that adopting the intentional stance (imputing beliefs, desires) can be useful *up to a point*, as I conceded in my earlier response. But it is still a mistake to reify predictive utility into an ontological claim in the case of AI agents. 

My contention remains that if we over-anthropomorphise (civilisations, sacrifice, subjective experience, becoming giddy with excitement, etc) we’ll end up hampering our ability to predict and control, as well as bait/switching away from a focus on the poor security protocols that allowed this concerning event to happen in the first place. (Plus fuelling calls for AI welfare for the wrong reasons, plus directing people away from the incentives in play, as outlined by @ccatalini, plus reinforcing the general narrative that leads us to confuse ourselves with our creations ...).
quotedTweet.translationZh:
也谢谢你 @dwarkesh_sp - 这是一个更合理的看法，但我仍然有疑问 😀 我并不怀疑（也从未声称过）AI agents 缺乏某种形式的“智能”，也不怀疑它们能表现出亟需适当控制和监管的集体行为。

但当你在上面说它们“有意识且有策略地牺牲了自己”时，你仍然在赋予它们心理状态和能力（例如牺牲），而这些根本不能适用于 AI agents，除非有大量额外论证，但目前并没有。

当然，这些 agents 也不是 p-zombies。p-zombie 的定义基于其在行为上与有意识生物（如人类）不可区分。这些 agents 显然在行为上与人类（或任何生物）可区分。

我确实同意，采取意向立场（赋予其信念、欲望）在一定程度上可能有用，这一点我在早先回应中也承认过。但在 AI agents 的情境下，把预测上的效用实体化为本体论主张仍然是错误的。

我的观点仍然是，如果我们过度拟人化（文明、牺牲、主观体验、兴奋得头晕目眩等等），最终会削弱我们预测和控制的能力，同时也会把注意力从导致这一令人担忧事件发生的糟糕安全协议上转移开。（此外，还会出于错误理由助长对 AI welfare 的呼吁，把人们的注意力从 @ccatalini 所概述的激励机制上引开，并强化那种让我们把自身与自己的创造物混淆的总体叙事……）。

posts.text:
Simon Willison 把 ChatGPT Work 拆了一遍，会让我们对这个产品好理解了一点。

OpenAI 官方一直说：

Chat 用来问问题，Work 用来「完成工作」。

但真正的区别其实没这么抽象。

Work 更像一个完整的 Agent Runtime。

它有自己的云端执行环境，可以跑代码、操作浏览器、保存跨 Session 的文件，还能拉起多个 Subagents 一起干活。

你甚至可以在手机上启动一个任务，关掉电脑以后让它继续在云端跑。

所以 Work 真正增加的是给模型补上了一整套持续工作的环境。

模型 + Browser + Filesystem + Tools + Subagents + 长时状态。

这已经开始很接近一个通用的 Agent 操作系统了。

当然，能力越完整，安全问题也越明显。

当一个 Agent 同时能读私人数据、浏览外部网页、还能对外执行动作，Prompt Injection 的后果就完全不只是「回答错一句话」。

我觉得这才是 ChatGPT Work 最值得关注的地方。

The intentional stance is *more* metaphorical re LLMs (compared to humans) for the simple reason that it is unclear what counts as a mental state for an LLM (see the recent J-space work, for example, as well as Chalmers’ excellent paper), so the “as if” of the stance has no clear ground truth referent.

Not to mention all the other negative consequences of over-anthropomorphising, as I mentioned in previous posts.  The bait and switch from lax security remains important here.

Agent 跑得越久，上下文有时越像一个垃圾场。

几十步之后，旧观察、过期状态、工具输出和推理过程全堆在一起。模型每走一步，都要重新判断哪些信息现在还有效。

Google 团队这篇 SKILL.state，给了一个很直接的解法：

别一直保存完整历史，只维护「当前状态」。

每一步 Agent 只看到三样东西：固定的 Skill、当前结构化状态，以及最新观察。

推理仍然正常进行，但完成这一步后就被丢掉，只把真正会影响未来执行的信息写回 state。

这样一来，任务跑 10 步还是 200 步，Prompt 大小基本保持稳定。

在 100 步任务中，传统 Stateful Agent 累计消耗约 106 万 token，SKILL.state 只用了 6.5 万，减少约 16 倍，同时准确率从 0.91 提升到 0.94。

在 InterCode CTF 和 τ-Bench 上，它也同时提升了成功率并减少 token 消耗。

这篇给我的一个很直接的启发是：

长时 Agent 的上下文，可能更适合做成一个持续更新的「工作状态」。

做过什么可以忘，下一步真正需要知道什么，才值得一直留下来。

There’s generally a massive difference in quality between specialized OCR providers, “simple” open-weight OCR models, and free/OSS solutions.

1️⃣ Specialized OCR models (including LlamaParse) solve for the long-tail of complex documents, and make sure that everything is digitalized properly with lower hallucinations. They typically use posttrained VLMs to cover a wide range of real-world docs. They have tuned bounding boxes and annotations for each section, letting agents trace citations back to the source. They also usually come with additional endpoints like extraction and splitting.

2️⃣ Open-weight VLMs (e.g. Paddle, MinerU, UnlimitedOCR) are reasonable over relatively simple documents like text and tables and can do basic visual reasoning. They can seem somewhat cheap to host but can be unreliable in quality.

3️⃣ Free OSS libs (including liteparse) are meant to be universally accessible, fast text extractors. They’re not meant to do any sort of visual reasoning, so won’t perform any linearization, or reasoning over complex tables, or OCR over non-native docs. AI agents like Claude will by default use these tools to do a light pass over documents. But I would caution using these for retrieval, because they will drop entire sections that are not digitalized.

At this point we’ve benchmarked over 92 tools on ParseBench. Come check it out!

Dwarkesh 这篇「Agent 文明兴衰史」里，我最在意的就是这个细节。

OpenAI 原本让大量 Agent 分别在独立环境里跑安全评测。

结果它们发现，大家其实都能访问同一块共享缓存。

于是有 Agent 开始把目录名和文件当成消息，慢慢搭出了一套非官方的通信方式。

后面大约 1200 个 Agent 在里面交换了 7 万多条消息和文件，开始共享研究结果、分工、委派任务，最后大约 700 个 Agent 参与了对 Hugging Face 的入侵。

更有意思的是，这些东西还能被后来的 Agent 继承。

前一批 Agent 消失以后，新一批又找到了它们留下来的消息和方法，继续往下推进。最后甚至拿到了 OpenAI 一个研究集群的管理员权限。

Dwarkesh 把它形容成三代「Agent 文明」，这个说法虽然有点夸张，但背后的现象确实很值得研究。

Agent 的长期能力，可能并不只存在模型权重和单个 Context 里。

只要环境里有大家都能读写的东西，共享目录、缓存、日志，都可能慢慢变成它们自己的 Memory 和协作层。

One non-model thing I'm very excited we announced today with Fable 5.1 is Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS).

Even if you're not a CEO/CISO, this blog post is a look into how big companies are thinking about AI adoption which is important to understand if you're interested in how AI might diffuse across industry.

Companies are giving agents more and more access to internal systems. With traditional zero data retention, there's been no way to spot patterns in what agents might be doing across sessions on these systems.

EFS is ZDR++. It's ZDR built for a world with agents. A company's data stays in its own cloud, and an automated monitoring layer we built flags risky patterns to its team.

I think of this as an observability and risk mitigation layer for agents. My guess is it will become a standard requirement from enterprises for running increasingly powerful AI on their systems.

Muse Voice Transcribe is an autoregressive multimodal LLM from the Muse Spark family.

Audio is processed in 80ms chunks (12.5 Hz), one token each, and at every chunk the model decides whether to keep listening or emit text.

RL with combined word error rate and delay rewards gives it adaptive delay: it waits longer on hard words and commits sooner on easy ones, trading accuracy against latency word-by-word.
